question.text: CALENDAR rebalancing (quarterly) vs THRESHOLD rebalancing (±5%) — key trade-off:

answer.text: Calendar = simpler, no interim monitoring but can be far from SAA on the rebalance date; Threshold = tighter control via trigger points but requires frequent monitoring

explanation.text: The Logic: Calendar rebalancing is simpler and does not require interim monitoring, but the portfolio may be close to — or far from — the SAA on the rebalance date. Threshold rebalancing uses trigger points to maintain tighter control over allocation, but it needs frequent monitoring to detect breaches. The Trap: Neither approach is universally "best" — the right choice depends on the IPS, cost tolerance and monitoring capacity. Note: The two methods can be combined, but the source emphasises the core trade-off between simplicity and tightness of control.
